requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

findings.claim: The acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T are honoured is not implemented. The no-surrogate path unconditionally builds a contractless model, ignoring [MessagePackObject], [Key], and [IgnoreMember] on the formatted type. For example, a [Key(0)] member is emitted under a string name key and an [IgnoreMember] property is still serialized.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedMessagePackFormatterReceiptTests.MessagePackAttributesOnReferencedTypeAreHonored. It uses an attributed type in a referenced assembly and expects an int-key array containing only the keyed member. On the submitted code it fails because the formatter instead emits a string-key map and includes the ignored Secret member.

findings.claim: Without a surrogate, MessagePack attributes already present on T are ignored: [MessagePackObject]/[Key] members are always converted to contractless string-key members. For example, a referenced [MessagePackObject] type whose only property is [Key(0)] is emitted with a map and the string key "Value" instead of an array with integer key 0, violating the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured. [IgnoreMember], member formatter attributes, and related annotations are bypassed by the same unconditional path.

receipt_plan.detail: Run MessagePackObjectKeysOnMetadataTypeAreHonored in tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/GeneratedFormatterCollectorReceiptTests.cs. Compile a metadata type with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)], generate its user-declared formatter, and inspect that formatter: the test requires WriteArrayHeader and rejects WriteMapHeader. On head the collector emits the contractless map formatter instead.

findings.claim: Serialization callbacks explicitly implemented by a base class of T produce uncompilable formatter code. hasCallbackReceiver includes inherited interfaces, but needsCast examines only T.GetMembers(); for a Derived : Base type where Base explicitly implements IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver, needsCast is false and the generated formatter calls value.OnBeforeSerialize()/OnAfterDeserialize() directly even though Derived has no accessible methods with those names.

receipt_plan.detail: Run ExplicitCallbacksInheritedFromBaseTypeRequireCast in tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/GeneratedFormatterCollectorReceiptTests.cs. Base explicitly implements both callback methods and Derived inherits Base; compiling the output of [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] for Derived must have no errors, but on head the generated direct callback calls produce CS1061 errors.

hunches.claim: When the formatted type itself carries MessagePack attributes, the new collector always takes its contractless or surrogate path and never reads those attributes. Consequently [Key] names/indices and [IgnoreMember] on T are ignored, producing a different wire contract instead of honouring the existing attributes as required.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator/serialization test with [MessagePackObject(true)] class Sample { [Key("renamed")] public int Value { get; set; } [IgnoreMember] public int Ignored { get; set; } } and [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class SampleFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<Sample>. Serialize new Sample { Value = 7, Ignored = 9 } using the generated formatter. The attributed contract should serialize as a one-entry map {"renamed":7}; the current contractless path instead generates entries for "Value" and "Ignored". Repeat with integer [Key] members to verify array keys are likewise honoured.

hunches.claim: The acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T are honoured is not met when no surrogate is supplied: the no-surrogate path always builds a contractless, string-keyed model from every public read-write member and never inspects MessagePackObject, Key, or IgnoreMember on T. An attributed external type therefore gets different keys and membership than its attributes specify.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an execution test whose external type is declared in a MessagePack-referencing fixture with [MessagePackObject], [Key(0)] on one member, and [IgnoreMember] on another public read-write member; generate a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] without SurrogateType and assert an integer-keyed array containing only the keyed member. The current CreateContractlessMembers path instead emits string keys and includes the ignored member.

hunches.claim: The tests do not cover the requirement that MessagePack attributes on T are honoured. The non-surrogate path always calls CreateContractlessMembers, so [Key] and [IgnoreMember] on T can be ignored while every added test still passes.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a formatter test for a T declared with [MessagePackObject], an integer [Key] member, and an [IgnoreMember] member. Assert that serialization uses the declared integer key and omits the ignored member; the current unconditional contractless path should fail this test.

hunches.claim: No test exercises the explicitly supported body-less formatter declaration (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`). Every positive fixture declares a braced body, so a regression in syntax discovery or generation for the semicolon form would go unnoticed.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L11] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: This feature is an explicit opt-in exception to the recorded default that metadata-only types are not analysed or formatted by the consuming assembly; it does not make the continuing absence of diagnostics or formatters for arbitrary referenced-assembly types a defect.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] records that referenced-assembly types deliberately receive no analysis or generated formatter by default. REQ-2129 deliberately adds generation only where the consuming assembly declares a class annotated with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter], leaving that default intact.

narrative: This run reviews reading A of REQ-2129 on branch review/ju26-issue-2129@verda/A: Implement the core feature together with the discussed surrogate-type mechanism so callers can specify keys and settings through a Project B surrogate when Project A cannot reference MessagePack. Code: In addition to the core generation support, expose a settable SurrogateType property on GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute and make the generator read the surrogate's members and attributes, mapping them to T's properties by name.
